15.1.title: From wild foods to policy innovation: MMSU's indigenous food plants program as a model for sustainable and inclusive agriculture
15.1.people: Menisa A. Antonio, Ma. Concepcion Birginias, Josefa Pugat, Maingeline Vivit, Ruby Rose Tamayo
15.1.summary: Best Paper, sustainable and smart agri-aquaculture and climate resilience category, 2025 SUC-ACAP Biennial Conference and General Assembly (27 to 29 August 2025, Tagbilaran City, Bohol). The paper covers conservation of wild food plants through in situ, ex situ and circa situ approaches and the adoption of the program by the Regional Development Council of Region 1.
15.1.note: Conference paper; Scopus indexing not checked.

detail.lead: MMSU's indigenous food plants paper won Best Paper at the 2025 SUC-ACAP conference, ahead of eight other papers in its category.

photos.caption: Partners receive indigenous food plant planting materials for the Community Foodscapes and Seedbanks, World Food Day 2025. (Photo: MMSU)
Farmers and local officials trained on alukon (himbabao) propagation, Brgy. 11 Sta. Rosa, Sarrat, 2 May 2025. (Photo: MMSU)

facts: 2025 SUC-ACAP Biennial Conference and General Assembly
27 to 29 August 2025, Metro Center Hotel, Tagbilaran City, Bohol
Sustainable and smart agri-aquaculture and climate resilience
Dr. Menisa A. Antonio, senior science research specialist, Research Directorate
Ma. Concepcion Birginias, Josefa Pugat, Maingeline Vivit, Ruby Rose Tamayo
Hosted with Bohol Island State University; 42 SUCs took part

p: The paper, "From wild foods to policy innovation: MMSU's indigenous food plants program as a model for sustainable and inclusive agriculture", describes the Indigenous Food Plants (IFP) program, which brings together conservation, innovation, policy and education. The program documented IFP species in Ilocos Norte and developed production technologies for crops such as himbabao (alokon), gac (sugodsugod) and latok (kapaskapas).

Conservation follows a triad of approaches: an IFP Botanical Garden (ex situ), a himbabao genebank at the MMSU Forest Reserve, circa situ cultivation of the wild yams kamangeg and dolian, and the integration of IFPs into community foodscapes. MMSU is also advancing omics-based molecular characterization to support conservation and use.
The IFP program is the first R&D initiative adopted by the Regional Development Council of Region 1, providing input for policy advocacy.

list: 2003: MMSU researchers surveyed five Ilocos Norte towns for vanishing plants and validated 77 using IUCN criteria.
2008 to 2010: survey and characterization of indigenous food plants in Ilocos Norte.
2011: SEARCA Discussion Paper No. 2011-2 documented 46 indigenous food plants from 27 families.
2019: Best Poster on the phenology of alukon at the Plant Biology Forum, UPLB.

15.1.title: Nature-based Solutions (NbS) for Sustainable Mangrove Management and Resilient Coastal Communities Through Innovative Green Engineering Approach
15.1.people: Dr. Arlene L. Gonzales (Project Leader), with DENR-PENRO Ilocos Norte, the Provincial Government and the LGUs of Badoc and Currimao
15.1.summary: DOST-PCAARRD-funded project (1 May 2024 to 30 April 2026) in Badoc and Currimao, Ilocos Norte. It addresses the poor hydrological conditions that keep young mangrove propagules from surviving, using technology-assisted plantations and bamboo-engineered structures.
15.1.note: Coastal ecosystem; the team may weigh it under SDG 14 as well.

15.1.title: Enhancing the productivity of rice-based cropping systems through soil health management (Project SLaM 2023/146)
15.1.people: Dr. Janet Villamor (MMSU project lead), with Griffith University, ACIAR and DOST-PCAARRD
15.1.summary: MMSU joined a five-year program to develop soil knowledge and capacity for more productive and sustainable cropping systems. It evaluates nutrient management and develops yield-calibrated soil health indices for rice-garlic, rice-rice and rice-onion systems in Ilocos Norte, Tarlac and Bataan.
15.1.note: Agricultural soil research; confirm it falls under THE's land-ecosystems keywords.

15.1.title: Characterization and Evaluation of Indigenous Food Plant Species
15.1.people: Menisa A. Antonio, Bjorn S. Santos, Maria Concepcion Birginias, Jomel Agreda, Bella Gervacio
15.1.summary: Study under the parent project "Strengthening the Resilience of Iloco Crop Diversity Through Complementary Conservation Approach", with related studies on ex situ conservation facilities and community foodscapes and seedbanks. Status: extended.

15.1.title: Documentation of Dipterocarp Species in Second Growth Forest of Ilocos Norte

15.1.title: Assessment and selection of suitable indigenous timber species under denuded hilly areas in Ilocos Norte
15.1.people: Charito Samsam, Sergia Garma, Joselito Rosario, Roseller Ayson

15.1.title: Phenology of Broussonetia luzonica (Blanco) Bur.: A Promising Indigenous Vegetable

15.1.summary: Documentation of dipterocarp trees dominating second-growth forests in Nueva Era, Pasuquin, Vintar, Adams and Pagudpud, with diameter, species and stocking data. Status: deferred.

15.1.people: Joselito Rosario, Charito Samsam, Dionisio Jamias, Sergia Garma

15.1.title: Survey and Characterization of Indigenous Food Plants in Ilocos Norte, Philippines
15.1.people: Menisa A. Antonio, Rodel T. Utrera, Epifania O. Agustin, Dionisio L. Jamias, Araceli J. Badar, Miriam E. Pascua
15.1.summary: SEARCA Agriculture and Development Discussion Paper No. 2011-2 (61 pages). Documented 46 indigenous food plants from 27 families in seven upland and remote municipalities, most of them wild species, and reported that MMSU maintains their germplasm as living plants and seeds.
15.1.note: Discussion paper; Scopus indexing not checked.

15.1.title: Survey and characterization of indigenous food plants in Ilocos Norte, Philippines
15.1.people: Menisa Antonio, Rodel T. Utrera, Epifania O. Agustin

15.1.title: MMSU researchers identify vanishing plant species
15.1.people: Dr. Miriam Pascua, Menisa Antonio, Dionisio Bucao and colleagues
15.1.summary: Survey of Laoag City, Batac, Pasuquin, San Nicolas and Dingras: of 124 plants that elders perceived to be vanishing, 77 were validated as such using IUCN criteria, 45 classified as endangered and 32 as vulnerable.
15.1.note: The classification applied IUCN criteria locally; it is not the IUCN Red List.

15.1.title: Natural Resources Conservation and Management Center (NRCMC)
15.1.people: Center Chief: Mae Ann R. Batuyong
15.1.summary: MMSU's research hub for the conservation of flora and fauna in the Ilocos Region. It leads R&D on plant genetic resources characterization, conservation of plants, animals and water resources, forest resource conservation and fishery resource management.

detail.lead: MMSU's research hub for the conservation of flora and fauna in the Ilocos Region, with work on plant genetic resources, forest resources and ecosystem assessment.

photos.caption: Image on the NRCMC page of the MMSU Research Directorate portal.

facts: Mae Ann R. Batuyong, PhD Biology (Plant Sciences Track)

p: The NRCMC envisions MMSU to become the research, promotion and conservation hub of flora and fauna in the Ilocos Region, working through inter-disciplinary, multi-sectoral and inter-agency collaboration and partnership. It spearheads R&D on plant genetic resources characterization, conservation of plants, animals and water resources, forest resource conservation and fishery resource management.
Its stated objective is to sustain natural resource health and services, and to establish in situ and ex situ conservation activities for Ilocos flora and fauna.

items.title: Phenological Assessment of Selected Indigenous Timber Species in Ilocos Norte
items.people: Charito Samsam, Joselito Rosario, Sergia Garma, Roseller Ayson
items.text: Develops a seed calendar for planting-stock production in rehabilitating denuded areas. Suggested collection windows: D. dao August to September, V. parviflora September to October, S. supa May to June, I. bijuga October to November, and A. thurifera April to May.

items.title: Evaluation of Suitable Indigenous Timber Species in Different Site Conditions
items.people: Charito Samsam, Joselito Rosario, Sergia Garma, Roseller Ayson, Bonne Jovi Orteza
items.text: Identifies promising species for rehabilitating denuded hilly areas in Ilocos Norte. Non-dipterocarps such as V. parviflora, W. pubescens, I. bijuga, S. supa and D. dao are recommended for open and degraded areas; dipterocarps such as H. plagata, A. thurifera and S. guiso are promising but need a compatible species mixture in early growth.

items.title: Fertilizer Management of Different Indigenous Timber Species Under Semi-Arid Hilly Area Condition
items.people: Charito Samsam, Joselito Rosario, Sergia Garma, Roseller Ayson, Bonne Jovi Orteza
items.text: Finds that 50 g of 14-14-14 plus 300 g of organic fertilizer was enough to improve the growth, biomass, vigor and survival of newly planted indigenous timber species on nutrient-poor hilly land.

items.title: Development of Propagation Management Technology for the Wild Vegetable Alokon (Broussonetia luzonica)
items.people: Maria Concepcion B. Birginias, Menisa A. Antonio, Josefa L. Pugat
items.text: Works out how to propagate alokon by stem cuttings, for domestication and for establishing duplicate mother trees at MMSU. Hormex as rooting hormone and 40 cm cuttings gave the highest survival.
